doc.title: Gene Bertoncini interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 13, 2001

title: Kraft Music Hall rhythm section, then learning bossa nova
summary: As classical guitar and bossa nova arrived he learned from Joao Gilberto's records and used it on an Ahmad Jamal date.

venues.name: That Was the Week That Was

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Playing with and understanding Thelonious Monk

blocks.x: Yeah. And during my tenure there for a whole year I did a show called “That Was the Week That Was,” for NBC and then occasionally the “Kraft Music Hall.” And the rhythm section for Peter Matz and the ‘Kraft Music Hall” was Derek Smith, Mel Lewis and Richard Davis and myself. And all the dates with Don Elliott in recording dates on Madison Avenue, it was always Mel Lewis and Richard Davis and myself. And boy I’ve been through a lot of — you know when you think about just falling into things. And I was a pretty good reader, not a great reader, but I mean I used to be able to cover whatever they wrote. And I guess my interpretation of things was what they liked as well. And then when I started playing the classical guitar I started getting — that was about the © Fillius Jazz Archive -8-

time the Bossa Nova came in. And I was very friendly with Joao Gilberto. He used to borrow my guitar to do concerts. And I learned how to do bossa nova from his records. And I just had barely started to play that way and I got a call from Ahmad Jamal to do a big date on Samba rhythms and I said, “Sure, I’ll do it.” And when I listen to Joao’s record of “Quiet Nights” and then I just took that little bit of information, the basic bossa nova beat, to Rudy VanGelder’s studio in New Jersey and it was Richard Evans’ big orchestra and Osie Johnson was playing drums and Richard. And it worked out great. I had — I just used to say yes, you know. I just figured, it seemed like you’re never called to do things that — you’re always called to do things that they know you can do.
Yeah, but you’ve also risen to the occasion, I can tell.
I think I have you know, but probably because I could, and not even realize it.
